direct_proof_arguments: The compact real S4 meets the positive plane transversely in one point, so its integral Borel-Moore class has infinite order.
A rotation of two b-coordinates swaps the two positive planes through a proper family of complex linear quadric automorphisms.
The exact polynomial homotopy (w,X(tw),tY(tw)) is proper because it retains w.
The actual closed source ring provides a polynomial lift of f1 on the ambient hypersurface.
The two principal-divisor cycles have respectively d sections plus B and the zero-section plane plus B, all with generic multiplicity one.
Their difference gives (d-1)alpha=0 in integral Borel-Moore homology, so d=1.
The retained rank classification then closes every constant trace; constant affine frames and offsets follow from the literal cotangent identity.
